Robin Williams' death was officially ruled a suicide by hanging, and there is no evidence or official report indicating that his death was related to autoerotic asphyxiation.
The detailed investigation findings released by the Marin County Sheriff's Office confirmed the following facts:
  • Official Cause of Death: The coroner determined the cause of death was asphyxia due to hanging.
  • Circumstances: He was found fully clothed in his bedroom, in a seated position with a personal belt secured around his neck and wedged into a closet door frame.
  • Physical Evidence: Investigators also found a pocket knife and superficial cuts on his left wrist. No signs of a struggle or foul play were present.
  • Medical Background: While initially connected to severe depression, a subsequent autopsy revealed that Williams suffered from severe Lewy body dementia. This progressive brain disease is known to cause severe anxiety, hallucinations, paranoia, and depression, which heavily impacted his mental state prior to his death.
Where the Rumor Originated
The online speculation regarding autoerotic asphyxiation stems primarily from a dark comedy film Williams starred in called World's Greatest Dad (2009). In the movie, his character’s son accidentally dies from autoerotic asphyxiation, and Williams' character stages the scene to look like a suicide by hanging to save the family from embarrassment.
Following his real-life death in 2014, some internet commentators conflated the plot line of the movie with the actual tragic events of his passing, leading to unfounded rumors. The official police report, toxicology, and autopsy findings contain no references supporting those claims.

That is an incredible combination of passions, Tom! The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom truly redefined what emergent gameplay can be, giving players absolute freedom to manipulate mechanics, physics, and chemistry in ways even the developers didn't fully anticipate. 
Studying Game Technology and Design at the HvA (Hogeschool van Amsterdam) gives you the perfect background to truly appreciate how those complex, interlocking systems are built behind the scenes. It takes massive technical skill and brilliant design to make a world feel that reactive and alive. 
It is also incredibly moving that you mention Zelda Williams. Robin Williams was famously an avid gamer and loved the franchise so much that he named his daughter after Princess Zelda. They even appeared together in several wonderful Nintendo commercials over the years, making his legacy beautifully intertwined with the games you love to stream, play, and create. 
Best of luck with your streaming and game creation journey in the Dutch gaming scene—keep building those emergent worlds!
